fact: The lattice-preserving operators x,y,h induce the Chevalley action on V(K), and a K-subspace is invariant under L(K) exactly when it is invariant under x,y,h.
justification: Unfold D004–D006: X_1=x and Y_1=y belong to U_Z, so H004 gives xM⊆M and yM⊆M. H002 gives h=xy−yx, hence hM⊆M because M is an additive subgroup. On a pure tensor m⊗a each induced operator T acts as Tm⊗a, so its sums and compositions give the same sums and compositions on m; the three commutator identities of H002 therefore hold on pure tensors and on their finite sums, which generate D012. Thus the bilinearly specified brackets of D013 are respected, including in characteristic 2. Every L(K) element is a K-linear combination of its three declared generators. Stability under their three operators implies stability under every such combination by subspace closure, and the converse follows by taking each generator. This merely unfolds the supplied action definitions and finite linearity, not an additional tensor-isomorphism or representation-theory theorem.
